title: Camera Path Spline Keyframe Editor with Particle Effects
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements a camera path spline keyframe editor with particle trail effects. Requirements:

## Scene Setup
- Dark background (0x111122) with a subtle grid floor (40x40, color 0x333355) at y=0.
- Place 5 landmark objects in the scene: colored boxes (size 1) at positions (-8,1,0), (-3,2,4), (0,1,-5), (5,3,2), (9,1,-3). Colors: red, green, blue, yellow, purple respectively.
- An orbit camera for the editor view, starting at position (0, 15, 25) looking at origin.
- Ambient light (0x404060) and a directional light (0xffffff, intensity 0.8) from (10,15,10).

## Spline Keyframe System
- Maintain an array of camera keyframes. Each keyframe stores: position (Vector3), lookAt target (Vector3), and a timestamp (seconds, starting from 0, auto-incrementing by 2s per keyframe).
- Start with 2 default keyframes: KF0 at position(-10,5,10) lookAt(0,0,0) t=0, KF1 at position(10,5,-10) lookAt(0,0,0) t=2.
- Build a CatmullRomCurve3 from keyframe positions. Render the spline as a visible tube geometry (radius 0.08, tubular segments 200, color 0x00ffaa).
- Render each keyframe as a small sphere (radius 0.3, color 0xff8800) at its position. The selected keyframe sphere should be color 0xffff00.

## Keyframe Editing
- Track a selectedKeyframeIndex (default 0).
- Press 'N' to add a new keyframe at the midpoint between the last keyframe position and (0,5,0), with timestamp = last keyframe time + 2s. Rebuild the spline.
- Press 'Delete' or 'Backspace' to remove the selected keyframe (minimum 2 keyframes must remain). Rebuild spline.
- Press 'Tab' to cycle selectedKeyframeIndex forward (wrap around).
- When a keyframe is selected, press arrow keys to move it: Left/Right move X by ±1, Up/Down move Z by ±1. Hold Shift with Up/Down to move Y by ±1. Rebuild spline on each move.

## Playback System
- A 'Play/Pause' button in the top-left UI panel. When playing, animate a preview camera marker (a small cone, color 0xff0044, height 0.6) along the spline based on elapsed time.
- Playback interpolates position along the spline using keyframe timestamps. Use linear interpolation between keyframe time segments mapped to spline parameter t.
- playbackSpeed = 1.0 by default. Press '+' to increase by 0.25 (max 3.0), '-' to decrease by 0.25 (min 0.25).
- When playback reaches the last keyframe time, loop back to start.
- Display current playback time in the HUD.

## Particle Trail Effect
- When playback is active, emit particles from the preview camera marker position.
- Maintain a particle pool of 300 particles (small spheres or use a Points system with BufferGeometry).
- Each particle spawns at the marker position with a small random velocity (range ±0.3 on each axis), has a lifetime of 1.5 seconds, and fades opacity from 1.0 to 0.0 over its lifetime.
- Particle color should match the spline color (0x00ffaa) with slight random hue variation.
- Track activeParticleCount in state.

## HUD / UI
- Top-left panel with: Play/Pause button, keyframe count display, selected keyframe index display, playback speed display, playback time display.
- A 'Reset' button that restores the 2 default keyframes and stops playback.
- Style buttons with dark semi-transparent background, white text, padding 8px.

## State Management
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
  - keyframeCount: number of keyframes
  - selectedKeyframeIndex: currently selected index
  - selectedKeyframePosition: {x,y,z} of selected keyframe
  - splinePointCount: number of points in the spline curve (use getPoints(200).length)
  - isPlaying: boolean
  - playbackTime: current playback time in seconds (0 if stopped)
  - playbackSpeed: current speed multiplier
  - previewMarkerPosition: {x,y,z} of the preview cone marker
  - activeParticleCount: number of currently alive particles
  - totalParticlesEmitted: cumulative count of particles spawned since last reset
  - splineTubeVisible: boolean, whether tube mesh is in scene and visible
  - keyframePositions: array of {x,y,z} for all keyframes
  - splineLength: total arc length of the CatmullRomCurve3 (use getLength())
physics_constraints: Particles must have finite positions (no NaN/Infinity). Particle lifetime must count down and particles must be recycled. Spline must be rebuilt whenever keyframes change. Playback time must loop correctly within [0, maxTime]. Keyframe timestamps must be monotonically increasing. Minimum 2 keyframes enforced at all times.
